plate_comment: Brake switch pair monitor, faults 394 = P0573 and 395 = P0572, run twice per 200 ms main loop cycle: switch 11 (the brake switch) and switch 2 (the second brake signal, DRB NOT BRAKE SWITCH; cruise denial and the governors treat the brake as applied when either is set) must agree. A state held for brake_switch_pair_debounce_threshold (15) passes with only switch 11 set counts one event toward fault 394, only switch 2 set toward fault 395, and an event count above brake_switch_pair_event_count_limit (15, so the 16th event) sets the fault; both-clear after both-set clears 394 and its count, both-set after both-clear clears 395 and its count, and the counts restart while the ignition key (switch 0) is off. Both faults are cleared on every pass while the monitor is disabled: operating_mode_flags_cal mask 0x2 clear, switch 11 without a hardware line, or switch 2 without a hardware line unless algorithm_enable_flags_6_cal mask 0x10 and cruise_control_switches_learned_flag are both set (was protection_enable_state_machine)
evidence: Fault 394 / 395 -> ROM 0x5985a slot 74 / 75 -> obd_dtc_code_table P0573 / P0572. The .cpp grep of every mask that touches them (0x400 / 0x800 set, 0xf3ff / 0xfbff / 0xf7ff clear on fault_detected_bits_384_to_399 / fault_registered_bits_384_to_399) finds only this function, and the nine state words are touched only here (sweep and .cpp name grep; no separate initializer or heal function was found, the heal is the 3 <-> 0 transition inside it). Switch 11 = brake: CCVS1 brake field, service_brake_* words, DRB 1A-02 mask 16 BRAKE SWITCH. Switch 2 is written only by cm848_scanAndDebounceSwitchInputs and by protection_j1939_control_logic (when it has no line), and the code ORs it with switch 11 as brake applied: cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor (2 sites), governor_cruise_deniedStatus_update, cm848_calculateProtectionSpeedLimits; DRB 1A-02 mask 32 is NOT BRAKE SWITCH (corroboration only: the same mask is EVAP PURGE SOLENOID for other engines, and a label does not give the polarity). The fault-clearing transitions 3 -> 0 / 0 -> 3 only make sense if both switches are set together when the brake is applied, so P0573 (circuit high) = switch 11 set while switch 2 is clear and P0572 (circuit low) = switch 2 set while switch 11 is clear. Values (RAM dump): threshold 15 at 0x408716, limit 15 at 0x408714; main_loop calls cm848_periodicTaskSet_outputs2 in phases 19 and 39 of 40. Truck dumps: switch_input_hardware_line_cal[2] (EEPROM 0x710) = 0 and cruise_control_switches_learned_flag (EEPROM 0x197e) = 0 in all three eeprom_dumps files, cm848_eeprom.bin and the RAM dump, so the gate is closed there, the function only clears 394 / 395 each pass, and fault_detected_bits_384_to_399 (0x3fe9a4) = 0.

plate_comment: Derives the second brake signal, logical switch 2 (DRB NOT BRAKE SWITCH), in software. It runs only while algorithm_enable_flags_6_cal mask 0x10 and cruise_control_switches_learned_flag are set and the ignition key (switch 0) is on. The trigger is the raw sample of switch 28 (inverted when second_brake_switch_idle_trigger_inverted_flag is set) while logical output 21 (the cruise servo supply request) is clear; while it is set, any serial output driver bit chosen by second_brake_switch_serial_driver_monitored_bits whose previously transmitted level matches second_brake_switch_serial_driver_expected_transmit_bits and whose status bit (xor second_brake_switch_serial_driver_status_polarity_bits) now differs from that level. An up / down accumulator (+1 per trigger pass up to second_brake_switch_trigger_accumulator_limit = 30, -1 per idle pass) latches second_brake_switch_trigger_confirmed_flag at the limit and releases it at 0, and when switch 2 has no hardware line (switch_input_2_hardware_line_cal = 0) that flag is written into mask 0x4 of switch_input_state_bits[0]. Called every other main loop phase (10 ms) from cm848_phase_group_a_processing (was protection_j1939_control_logic)
evidence: Nothing in it reads J1939: the old name came from protection_j1939_mode_enable_flag, which is the switch 2 hardware line word (lhz 4 off the switch_input_hardware_line_cal base 0x3fdb8e, same base as the lhz 22 of qadc_init_done_flag). The .cpp name grep shows it as the only writer of switch_input_state_bits[0] besides the scan function (the sweep missed its store, so the sweep alone is not proof); the scan leaves a switch with no line and no datalink bit at its current state, so switch 2 follows this function on this calibration. Output 21 test = logical_output_request_bits byte 2 mask 0x20 (request 21, the cruise servo supply). Byte widths from disasm_func.py (lbz) and the RAM dump values: monitored 0x09, expected 0x09, polarity 0x00, idle inversion 0x00, limit 30, step 1, previous transmit byte 0. What switch 28 (hardware line 22) and serial driver bits 0 / 3 (lines 152 / 155) are wired to is not established, so the name makes no wiring claim. In every dump the outer gate is closed (learned flag 0), so it does nothing there.

Counts consecutive passes in the state switch 11 set / switch 2 clear (bVar1 = 1) while the previous debounced state is not 1; every other state clears it; at brake_switch_pair_debounce_threshold it adds one event to the 0x40b1fe count. Word (sth / lhz), working RAM, no _cal.
Same as 0x3fcd84 for the state switch 2 set / switch 11 clear (bVar1 = 2); at the threshold it adds one event to the 0x40b200 count. Word, working RAM, no _cal.

Counts consecutive passes with both switches clear (bVar1 = 0); at the threshold it resets itself, stores previous state 0 and, if the previous state was 3, clears fault 394 and the switch-11-only event count. Word, working RAM, no _cal.

Counts consecutive passes with both switches set (bVar1 = 3); at the threshold it resets itself, stores previous state 3 and, if the previous state was 0, clears fault 395 and the switch-2-only event count. Word, working RAM, no _cal.

Last debounced state of the pair: 0 = both clear, 1 = switch 11 only, 2 = switch 2 only, 3 = both set; updated only when a state has been held for the debounce threshold. Byte (lbz / stb), working RAM, no _cal.

Debounced entries into the state switch 11 set / switch 2 clear; when it exceeds brake_switch_pair_event_count_limit fault 394 (P0573) is set and the count is clamped to the limit; reset by the 3 -> 0 transition and by a key-off. Word, working RAM, no _cal.
Debounced entries into the state switch 2 set / switch 11 clear; above the limit fault 395 (P0572) is set; reset by the 0 -> 3 transition and by a key-off. Word, working RAM, no _cal.

lhz @ 0x5122c4 / 0x5122ec / 0x512380 / 0x5123a8: both event counts are compared with it (count above it sets the fault); value 15 in the RAM dump, so the 16th event sets the fault. Never written (RAM-resident constant), outside the EEPROM mirror: no _cal.

lhz @ 0x512298 / 0x512354 / 0x5123fc / 0x5124a4: every debounce count of the pair is compared with it; value 15 in the RAM dump (15 passes of 100 ms = 1.5 s). RAM-resident constant, outside the EEPROM mirror: no _cal.

The application reads it as lhz 22(r30) with r30 = the switch_input_hardware_line_cal base 0x3fdb8e, i.e. entry 11 (0x3fdb8e + 2 x 11), the brake switch's discrete input line: 147 in the RAM dump (the 11:147 of the line map) and in EEPROM 0x722 (0x70c + 22); 0 would mean no line. protection_enable_state_machine disables itself when it is 0 and cm848_j1939BuildEngineStatusByte reports Aux I/O #02 as not available. EEPROM mirror range, so _cal, following the switch_input_13_hardware_line_cal pattern. Keep the boot role in the comment: TIME-SHARED, during boot / reflash the CMF flash driver (mpc555_cmfEraseBlocks, ...ApplyHighVoltagePulse, ...EndHighVoltagePulse, ...RestoreNormalMode, ...SelectBlockAndStartSequence, byte loads) uses the byte at this address as its test step count and mpc555_initHardwareConfig stores it.

Read as lhz 4(r30) with the same base 0x3fdb8e by protection_enable_state_machine and cm848_j1939BuildEngineStatusByte (and by absolute address in protection_j1939_control_logic): entry 2, the discrete input line of switch 2. EEPROM 0x710 = 0 in every dump (no line); the old comment (ROM flag gating J1939-triggered protection mode bit 2) is wrong: it is EEPROM-backed (inside 0x3fd482-0x3feec1) and nothing about J1939. When it is 0 the feeder writes switch 2's state in software and the monitor needs the cruise-learned gate instead. Never written in the application.
Set each pass by cm848_deriveSecondBrakeSwitchSignal from the switch 28 sample or the serial output driver mismatch test; cleared with the key off. Byte, working RAM, no _cal.
Up / down debounce accumulator of the trigger: + step per active pass (kept below 0x100, limit-clamped), -1 per inactive pass, 0 with the key off. Byte, working RAM, no _cal.

Set when the accumulator reaches its limit, cleared when it has decayed to 0; written into mask 0x4 of switch_input_state_bits[0] (switch 2) when switch 2 has no hardware line. Byte, working RAM, no _cal.
RAM-resident constant read by the feeder as the accumulator ceiling / confirm level; value 30 (0x1e) in the RAM dump; 30 passes of 10 ms = 0.3 s. No _cal.
RAM-resident constant added to the accumulator per active pass; value 1 in the RAM dump. No _cal.

DAT_003fcd8d: lbz @ 0x511fdc, stb @ 0x5120f0 (disasm_func.py, both in cm848_deriveSecondBrakeSwitchSignal): copy of serial_output_driver_transmit_byte at the end of each pass, compared bit by bit with the next status byte; 0 in the RAM dump. Working RAM in the copy window: no _cal.
DAT_00408718: lbz @ 0x511fd4; bit i selects serial output driver bit i for the mismatch test; 0x09 in the RAM dump (bits 0 and 3 = output lines 152 and 155). RAM-resident constant: no _cal.

DAT_00408719: lbz @ 0x511fcc; bit i must equal the previously transmitted level of bit i for the test to count (the level at which the driver output is checked); 0x09 in the RAM dump. RAM-resident constant: no _cal.
DAT_0040871a: lbz @ 0x511fbc; xor-ed into serial_output_driver_status_byte before it is compared with the previously transmitted level; 0x00 in the RAM dump. RAM-resident constant: no _cal.
DAT_0040871b: lbz @ 0x511f74; when nonzero the trigger taken from the switch 28 sample (logical output 21 clear) is inverted; 0x00 in the RAM dump. RAM-resident constant: no _cal.

text: [W10 switches, lead 1] AUXIO1: cm848_j1939BuildEngineStatusByte (0x24028), cm848_initJ1939EngineStatusBuffer (0x24124) and j1939_pgn65269_tx_data are the ECM's own PGN 65241 Auxiliary Input/Output Status 1 message (header constant 0x14fed9; local j1939 DB: byte 1 bits 7-8 Aux I/O #01, 5-6 #02, 3-4 #03, 1-2 #04), not an engine status byte and not PGN 65269 (AMB): #01 = switch 19 (not available when the word at 0x3fdbb4 is 0: that is qadc_control_word_cal._2_2_, entry 19 of the same line table, 0x3fdb8e + 2 x 19, EEPROM 0x732, value 148), #02 = switch 11 (not available when switch_input_11_hardware_line_cal = 0), #03 = switch 2 (not available when switch_input_2_hardware_line_cal = 0), #04 = always not available. It uses the two renamed line words exactly like the monitor does. Misname lead for a later wave (rename to an AUXIO1 name, and the PGN 65269 labels of its buffer), not done here because it is not part of the P0572 / P0573 group. The other qadc_control_word_* rows (0x3fdbb2 dword = entries 18-19, 0x3fdbb6 dword = 20-21, 0x3fdbba = 22, 0x3fdbbe = 24, 0x3fdbc2 = 26, 0x3fdbc6 = 28, 0x3fdbca = 30) are entries of the same switch_input_hardware_line_cal table (time-shared with the boot CMF erase value array): candidates for switch_input_<n>_hardware_line_cal names later (the dword rows would need a type change, so only a note here).

[W10 switches, lead 1] Callers keep their names because they schedule unrelated work: cm848_periodicTaskSet_outputs2 (0xc078, main_loop phases 19 and 39) also runs cm848_outputs2_periodic and cm848_monitorConverterClutchAndOverdrivePerformance; cm848_phase_group_a_processing (0xb7b4, every even phase) runs the feeder among dozens of tasks. No separate initializer or heal function was found for the brake pair: its state words are written only by the monitor.

[W10 switches, lead 1] Dump facts and a bench check: in every dump cruise_control_switches_learned_flag (EEPROM 0x197e) = 0 and switch_input_hardware_line_cal[2] = 0, so the monitor and the derived switch 2 are both off (both use the same gate: algorithm_enable_flags_6_cal = 0x801f has mask 0x10 set, operating_mode_flags_cal = 0x7ca6 has mask 0x2 set). Once the flag becomes 1 (first valid cruise ON/OFF press) both switch on together; then the pair only agrees if the derived switch 2 follows switch 11. Bench: while pressing the brake read switch_input_state_bits (RAM 0x40c050) byte 0 mask 0x4 (switch 2) against byte 1 mask 0x8 (switch 11); the monitor sets P0573 after 16 debounced states with only switch 11 set. Polarity (bytewise, polarity[switch >> 3]): the polarity bits of switch 2 (byte 0 mask 0x4) and switch 11 (byte 1 mask 0x8) in EEPROM 0x708 are 0, so neither switch is inverted. The name pattern switch_input_<n>_hardware_line_cal could be applied to the other entries of the 32-word table that still have unrelated names (not checked here).

plate_comment: Fuel level low distance monitor, fault 398 = P0461 plus the internal fault 397 (no DTC slot), evaluated on every 4th call, i.e. every 0.8 s when it is called once per 200 ms main loop cycle (phase 6). After each key-on edge it waits 19 evaluations (about 15 s, fuel_level_low_distance_check_start_delay_limit = 18), and it is switched off until the next key-on while the fuel level sensor substitutes a fault value (fuel_level_fault_substitution_flag). When armed (fuel_level_low_distance_check_armed_flag_cal) and enabled (protection_feature_status_flags mask 0x20, operating_mode_flags_cal mask 0x4), a stored fuel level byte (eeprom_shadow_header.calibration_block1[1], 1/2.55 % per count) below fuel_level_low_distance_level_threshold (38 = 14.9 %) sets fault 397 and adds vehicle_speed x 222 >> 4 to fuel_level_low_distance_accumulator_cal; at or above the threshold the fault and the accumulator clear. Above fuel_level_low_distance_accumulator_limit (1920000000, about 120 miles) it sets fault 398 = P0461, clears 397 and disarms; P0461 clears and re-arms when the stored level is above the threshold again, and fault 397 also clears while P0462 / P0463 (faults 382 / 381) are active (was cm848_main_loop_protection_eval)
evidence: Fault 398 -> ROM 0x5985a slot 87 -> P0461; fault 397 -> slot 170 (no DTC); faults 381 / 382 -> slots 85 / 86 -> P0463 / P0462 (read from the ROM tables, not the CSV comment). The whole function is this monitor: its state words (0x3fd1cc-0x3fd1d0, 0x3fee9c / 0x3fee9e, 0x409ec6-0x409ed0) are used only by it and by the initializer at 0x5305dc (.cpp name grep plus sweep), and no other mask clear or set of 0x2000 / 0x4000 on fault_detected_bits_384_to_399 exists in the .cpp. Units: the stored level is the byte at 0x3fee19 (lbz) written by cm848_filterFuelLevelSlow / cm848_qualifyFuelLevelSample (dump 0xfc = 252 = 98.8 %); vehicle_speed is 1/256 mph; per evaluation the accumulator gains v x 3552 (v in mph), i.e. 222 / 16 x 256 x 3600 / 0.8 s = 15,984,000 per mile, so 1,920,000,000 = 120.1 miles. That distance rests on the 0.8 s period (main_loop calls the function only in phase 6 of 40 five-millisecond phases, every 4th call, as in cm848_advanceHourMeters' 0.2 s cycle). Reading: a tank cannot run 120 miles on its last 15 %, so a level stuck that low is implausible, consistent with the P0461 range / performance title (inference). Dumps: armed flag = 1 and accumulator = 0 in every EEPROM dump (0x1a1a / 0x1a1c) and the RAM dump, fault_detected_bits_384_to_399 = 0; protection_feature_status_flags is 0x06ff4040 in the RAM dump (mask 0x20 clear), so the accumulation gate was closed there.

plate_comment: Start-up state of the fuel level low distance monitor: sets the pass count (fuel_level_low_distance_check_pass_count) to 4 so the first pass evaluates, disables the check until the first key-on edge, clears the previous key-on flag and the start delay done flag, and clears fault 397 (detected and registered). Called once from cm848_applicationMain (was cm848_initialization_group37_state)
evidence: Body read: stores 4 / 1 / 0 / 0 into 0x3fd1cc / 0x3fd1cd / 0x3fd1ce / 0x3fd1cf and clears mask 0xdfff of fault_detected_bits_384_to_399 and fault_registered_bits_384_to_399; cm848_applicationMain case 100 calls it beside the other cm848_initialization_group*_state calls. It does not touch the delay count, the armed flag or the accumulator (those persist or have no initializer here).

Incremented on every pass (one call of the monitor per 200 ms main loop cycle); above 3 it resets to 0 and the check runs, so the check runs on every 4th pass; the initializer sets 4 so the first pass evaluates. Byte (lbz / stb), working RAM, no _cal.

1 after the initializer and at key-off, set to 1 again while fuel_level_fault_substitution_flag is 1, cleared only at a key-on edge; the distance check runs only while it is 0 (read once, lbz @ 0x5307b8). Not a 'previous' value and not a protection-mode output. Byte, working RAM, no _cal.
Ignition key state (switch 0) of the previous evaluation; a 0 -> 1 edge restarts the start delay and clears the disabled flag. Byte, working RAM, no _cal.
Set when the start delay count has reached its limit while the key is on, cleared at key-off and by the initializer; the whole check below it only runs when it is set. Byte, working RAM, no _cal.
Zeroed at each key-on edge, +1 per evaluation while the key is on, held at the limit; one count = 0.8 s. Word (lhz / sth), working RAM, no _cal.
lhz @ 0x5306f8; value 18 in the RAM dump; the done flag sets on the evaluation after the count reached it (19 evaluations, about 15 s). RAM-resident constant, outside the EEPROM mirror: no _cal.

Word at 0x3fee9c = EEPROM 0x1a1a (0x3fee9c - 0x3fd482), inside the EEPROM mirror, so it needs _cal under the rule used for the persisted counts of the P0500 monitor (the old comment says 'no _cal' for EEPROM-backed state); value 1 at EEPROM 0x1a1a in all three eeprom_dumps files and in the RAM dump. Word order brought in line with the other fuel_level_low_distance_* names.

Dword at 0x3fee9e = EEPROM 0x1a1c, inside the EEPROM mirror (saved with the 0x8ea-0x1a3d block, so the distance carries across key cycles): _cal. lwz @ 0x53086c / 0x5308ac; 0 in every dump. Word order brought in line with fuel_level_low_distance_level_threshold / _vehicle_speed_scale.

DAT_00409ec8: lwz @ 0x5308b4 (disasm_func.py, dword); the accumulator is compared with it and fault 398 (P0461) is set above it; 1920000000 (0x7270e000) in the RAM dump = about 120 miles at the 0.8 s evaluation period. Already quoted in the comments of 0x3fee9e / 0x409ec6 / 0x409ecc. RAM-resident constant, outside the EEPROM mirror: no _cal.

text: [W10 switches, lead 2] Struct field, not renamed here: eeprom_header_t.calibration_block1 (6 bytes at 0x3fee18, EEPROM 0x1996 in the application's mirror use of the time-shared header) is the stored fuel level: byte [0] fast filter, [1] slow filter (the byte this monitor reads, 0x3fee19), [2] copy; dumps hold fc fc fc. Suggested field name stored_fuel_level (comment: time-shared with the boot ROM header shadow).

[W10 switches, lead 2] Left alone on purpose: the other protection_eval_* rows (protection_eval_step_index, _frame_counter, _sub_counter, _step_count, _rpm_upper_cal, _rpm_lower_cal, _frame_limit_cal, protection_eval_state) are not touched by this function or its initializer. cm848_main_loop_protection_eval was called directly from main_loop (phase 6), so there is no caller to keep or rename; its group is the monitor plus the initializer cm848_initialization_group37_state, whose caller cm848_applicationMain does unrelated work. Gate words shared by many monitors and still to review (task 044): mask 0x20 of protection_feature_status_flags (0x40b9d0) and mask 0x4 of operating_mode_flags_cal (0x7ca6 in the dumps, set).

plate_comment: Background checksum of the calibration and the code, one 100-byte chunk (rom_crc_bytes_per_pass) per call, called from cm848_periodicTaskGroup37_calibration16 twice per 200 ms main loop cycle (about 11 minutes for everything after power-up). rom_crc_calc_phase 0 / 1 runs a CRC16 (cm848_calculateCrc16Simple: table-driven, table at ROM 0x5842e, seed 0, no final xor) over the EEPROM-mirror calibration block 0x3fd59a-0x3fd5f3 (EEPROM 0x118-0x171) into rom_crc_computed_results[0]; phase 2 / 3 does ROM 0x8000-0x6fc61 plus flash2 0x500000-0x53ea6d into rom_crc_computed_results[1] (segment tables at flash2 0x53ac3c / 0x53ac2a); phase 4 = done. Each result is compared with the stored word in the EEPROM (rom_crc_stored_calibration_result_cal at EEPROM 0x482, rom_crc_stored_code_result_cal at 0x484) and a mismatch sets fault 357 = P0602 (control module programming error); the two results are also the OBD mode 9 PID 6 calibration verification number (cm848_processPciObdRequest, answered only once phase 4 is reached) (was governorSpeedLimitTable)
evidence: Fault 357 -> ROM 0x5985a slot 104 -> P0602. Reproduction 1, originals/cm848_ram.bin: rom_crc_calc_phase (0x40b66c) = 4 and the results 0x88ef / 0xa0fa (0x40b66e / 0x40b670) equal the stored pair at 0x3fd904 / 0x3fd906; cm848_eeprom.bin holds the same pair at EEPROM 0x482 / 0x484; fault bit 357 is clear in that dump (0x3fe9a0 = 0x0010). Reproduction 2, offline: the CRC loop of cm848_calculateCrc16Simple (0x55ea0: c = (c >> 8) ^ table[(c ^ byte) & 0xff], table of 256 words at ROM 0x5842e, entries 0x1189 0x2312 0x329b ..., i.e. the reflected 0x1021 table, seed 0) over EEPROM 0x118-0x171 gives 0x88ef for cm848_eeprom.bin and 0x5e0e for each of before_hpt, after_hpt_1 and after_hpt_2, equal to the stored word at EEPROM 0x482 in all four files. Ranges decoded from flash2: 0x53ac2a = 0x00008000, 0x0006fc61, 0x00500000, 0x0053ea6d (count word 2 at 0x53ac28) and 0x53ac3c = 0x003fd59a, 0x003fd5f3 (count word 1 at 0x53ac3a); 0x3fd59a - 0x3fd482 = 0x118 and 0x3fd5f3 - 0x3fd482 = 0x171, so the first range is the EEPROM mirror, not ROM. DAT_00408de0 = 100 bytes per call; 681,680 bytes / 100 per call at 10 calls per second = about 680 s (cm848_periodicTaskGroup37_calibration16 sits in main_loop phases 12 and 32 of 40). The state words are written only here (.cpp name grep; the other users are the OBD mode 9 reads of phase and results), and no clear of mask 0x20 on fault_detected_bits_352_to_367 was found, so the fault is set here and left to the common fault clearing. The three files in eeprom_dumps (before_hpt, after_hpt_1, after_hpt_2) hold a different stored pair, 0x5e0e / 0x6231, from cm848_eeprom.bin and the RAM dump (0x88ef / 0xa0fa); their calibration blocks differ in exactly one byte, EEPROM 0x135 (0x24 in cm848_eeprom.bin, 0x20 in the three others: the low byte of fault_feature_config_flags at 0x3fd5b6, mask 0x4 cleared).

lhzx @ 0x52454c (disasm_func.py: indexed array base 0x3fd904, index = rom_crc_result_index x 2): stored expected CRC16 of the EEPROM calibration block 0x3fd59a-0x3fd5f3; 0x3fd904 - 0x3fd482 = EEPROM 0x482, inside the mirror: _cal. 0x88ef in cm848_eeprom.bin and the RAM dump, 0x5e0e in the three eeprom_dumps files; each equals the CRC16 of EEPROM 0x118-0x171 of its own file (recomputed offline). Never written by the application (EEPROM-loaded).

Second element of the same indexed lhzx (index 1): stored expected CRC16 of ROM 0x8000-0x6fc61 plus flash2 0x500000-0x53ea6d, EEPROM 0x484, _cal. 0xa0fa in cm848_eeprom.bin and the RAM dump, 0x6231 in the three eeprom_dumps files (not recomputable offline: see the segment table note).

Second word of rom_crc_computed_results: stored through (&rom_crc_computed_results)[rom_crc_result_index] by the CRC check (result index 1 = ROM + flash2) and read as DAT_0040b670 (lhz) in the mode 9 PID 6 reply of cm848_processPciObdRequest (bytes 6-7 of the calibration verification number); 0xa0fa in the RAM dump. Working RAM: no _cal.
DAT_00408de0: lhz in the CRC check, the chunk length added to rom_crc_scan_ptr each call; 100 in the RAM dump. RAM-resident constant, outside the EEPROM mirror: no _cal.

text: [W10 switches, lead 3] The two flash2 segment tables (0x53ac2a: 2 segments of start / end dwords, only 2-byte aligned; 0x53ac3c: 1 segment) are reached only through rom_crc_descriptor_table_ptr (dword loads through a pointer), so there is no direct load width for a new_global row; the decompile shows them as &DAT_0053ac2a / &DAT_0053ac3c. The code CRC range ends at flash2 0x53ea6d, but cm848_flash2_live.bin is 0x3e000 bytes and ends at 0x53dfff, so about 2.7 KB (2,670 bytes, 0x53e000-0x53ea6d) of the checked range is not in the dump and the second CRC cannot be recomputed offline. The existing rom_crc_* names (calc_phase, scan_ptr, descriptor_table_ptr, accumulator, segment_index, segment_count, result_index, iteration_count, computed_results) stay: they are accurate, only the prefix is loose because the first range is the EEPROM calibration block. If symmetric names are wanted next to the new 0x40b670 row, rename 0x40b66e rom_crc_computed_results to rom_crc_computed_calibration_result.

[W10 switches, lead 3] Consequence for flashing, verified for the first CRC: EEPROM 0x118-0x171 (the feature flag words, e.g. algorithm_enable_flags_6_cal at EEPROM 0x126, fault_feature_config_flags at 0x134, operating_mode_flags_cal at 0x16c) is protected by the word at EEPROM 0x482, and a tuning tool has already kept the pair consistent: the single changed byte at EEPROM 0x135 (0x24 -> 0x20) comes with the stored word 0x88ef -> 0x5e0e, which the CRC reproduces. Any other edit inside that block needs the word at EEPROM 0x482 recomputed (the loop above), otherwise the code sets P0602 (fault 357) at the next power-up check; no mismatch case occurs in any dump. The same holds for ROM / flash2 content against EEPROM 0x484, which could not be checked offline. The caller cm848_periodicTaskGroup37_calibration16 (0xbf60) also runs cm848_calibration_group37_load and hpcr_injectPressureDiagnostic, so it keeps its name.
